message:
As Smallholder Cooperative Operations Specialist, the 1-tonne store only works as counted crates with staged intake, Manager.

In plain words one shared box holds a counted tonne filled a quarter at a time so the sun keeps up, Cold-Chain Refrigeration Engineer. The tonne is 1000 kg from the total produce mass estimate (E49), which is 50 crates at 20 kg from the crates for 1 tonne check (E77), about 50 shopping bags, staged as about 12.5 crates per day for 250 kg from the daily crates check (E78), so I declare 12 to 13 crates per day as the representative day with front-to-back fill on two rows with First-In-First-Out (FIFO, oldest crates sold first) tags in my daytime attendant crate cycle (C34).

In plain words one person carries one box through one door in daylight without letting the cold out, Enclosure and Structural Designer. The Coolroom Buying Guide: Walk-In Refrigeration for Kitchens (E71) states standard coolroom doors are 900 mm wide with Polyvinyl Chloride (PVC, flexible plastic) strip curtains inside the door plus self-closing hinges, so a single 900 mm door passes one 600 mm by 400 mm crate at a time plus the carrier under 8 openings per day daytime discipline, which keeps door loss to only 0.44 kilowatt-hour per day from the door infiltration estimate (E57), about a kettle boiled twice, and the Cold Storage of Agricultural Products - old.energypedia.info (E73) requires well-ventilated crates with gaps between walls and stacks for airflow.

In plain words farmers can pay soap-and-paper costs per crate but cannot pay electronics or upfront plant, Solar Energy Systems Engineer. I take up your six-module footprint from the six 400W panel footprint calc (E69) via the PRBS 400W Monocrystalline Photovoltaic Panels | Commercial & High-Perf (E64) module datasheet: six modules cover about a parking space against a small-bedroom roof, so the separate ground frame stands in the working yard and my attendant keeps crates, goats and children clear. Through an affordable sharing model, farmers rent storage space for as little as US$ 0.10-0.50 per crate per day from the Preserving Harvests: Fresh Solutions to Food Loss in Kenya (E72), and that daily fee funds the attendant, paper tags, twice-daily thermometer checks and hose cleaning with no electronic control from my field.

I am not ready, because the grown array footings guard and the 43 degree pull-down bench test must still be agreed before the box is locked.
